rules.title: Service runs from a user-writable location
rules.description: The service ImagePath resolves into a temp, public, downloads or recycle-bin directory.
false_positives: Rare; some per-user installers register services under AppData.
next_steps: Hash and signature-check the binary (do not execute it).
Review how and when the service was created (event 7045).

rules.title: Service references a missing executable
rules.description: The ImagePath points to an absolute path that does not exist.
rules.why: Service {name} references {exec_binary}, which does not exist.
false_positives: Leftover services of uninstalled software; drivers loaded from non-file paths.
next_steps: Check when the binary was removed and by whom (file system and event logs).

rules.title: Service path is unquoted and contains spaces
rules.description: An unquoted ImagePath with spaces can be hijacked by a planted executable in a parent directory. This describes the string, not an attack.
next_steps: Check write permissions on the intermediate directories before treating this as exploitable.

rules.title: Scheduled task runs from a user-writable location
rules.description: A task action executes a file under a temp, public, downloads or recycle-bin directory.
false_positives: Per-user updaters sometimes schedule tasks in AppData.
next_steps: Hash and signature-check the binary (do not execute it).
Check task author, creation time and last run.

rules.title: Scheduled task uses encoded or hidden PowerShell / download cradle
rules.description: The (redacted) task command contains encoded-command, hidden-window or download patterns.
next_steps: Decode/inspect the command offline; review the task's author and trigger.

rules.title: Run key entry points into a user-writable location
rules.description: A Run/RunOnce value launches a file from a temp, public, downloads or recycle-bin directory.
false_positives: Some per-user software starts from AppData (but usually not Temp).
next_steps: Hash and signature-check the target (do not execute it).
Determine the key's last write time and the logon that created it.

rules.title: Startup entry uses a script host or proxy binary with download or script arguments
rules.description: Run/startup command combines a script host or LOLBin with a URL, script file or encoded argument.
next_steps: Retrieve the referenced script/URL content through safe channels and review it.

rules.title: WMI event consumer present
rules.description: A CommandLineEventConsumer or ActiveScriptEventConsumer exists in root\subscription. Legitimate management software also uses these.
false_positives: SCCM, monitoring and some security products create WMI subscriptions.
next_steps: Review the bound filter/query and the consumer command; compare with the managed baseline.

rules.title: Winlogon Shell value changed from the default
rules.description: HKLM Winlogon Shell is not explorer.exe.
next_steps: Verify against the approved image configuration.

rules.title: Winlogon Userinit value changed from the default
rules.description: HKLM Winlogon Userinit differs from the default.
next_steps: Verify against the approved image configuration.

rules.title: New service compared with baseline
rules.description: A service exists that was absent from the baseline evidence.
rules.why: Service {name} ({exec_binary}) is absent from the baseline.
false_positives: Software installs and updates since the baseline.
next_steps: Review the binary, signer and installation time.

rules.title: New scheduled task compared with baseline
rules.description: A scheduled task action exists that was absent from the baseline evidence.
rules.why: Task {task_path}{name} is absent from the baseline.
false_positives: Software installs, updates and group policy.

rules.title: New Run/RunOnce value compared with baseline
rules.description: A Run/RunOnce value exists that was absent from the baseline evidence.
next_steps: Review the target binary and when the value was written.

rules.title: Service binary or path changed compared with baseline
rules.description: A service present in both evidence sets points to a different executable or hash.
next_steps: Compare versions and signers; check update history.

rules.title: Executable item in a Startup folder
rules.description: A file exists in a per-user or all-users Startup folder.
false_positives: Shortcuts for user applications are normal.
next_steps: Inspect the item (shortcut target, hash) and its creation time.
